The renderer is inherited from the PS Vita version: texture cache, opaque batches, baking. This is normally the fastest mode; if the picture looks wrong (black or missing sprites), turn it off — every optimisation is then disabled through marker files next to data.win.
Draw without the game\'s shaders (on by default)

The workaround this build ships with: every sprite is drawn with a plain program, so the palette swaps the game\'s shaders do (enemies, bosses and bullets change colour with them) are missing, but nothing disappears. Turn it off to get the palette swaps back; a sprite that then goes missing or breaks is drawn wrong by its own shader.
Off: the pad behaves like a real controller, and the game shows controller prompts. On: every button also presses its keyboard key (the game then draws keyboard prompts).

A fan port of Angry Video Game Nerd 8-bit to Android, made from the PS Vita port of the same game. It contains no game files: you import your own data.win, fonts and cutscene videos, and the app runs the game through Butterscotch, a free GameMaker runtime (AGPL-3.0). Neither this port nor the Vita one distributes the game.

Import the game folder or a zip archive with the Import button. The APK is published in the artifacts of the workflow run only: Actions → Android APK → the run → Artifacts → AVGN8bit-apk. The port does not make releases. A new build installs over the previous one: the imported game files and the settings stay in place, no uninstall is needed.

PS Vita and Android run the same Butterscotch fork: the same data.win parser, the same GML virtual machine and renderer, including the fast paths written for the Vita (texture cache, opaque batching, baked CRT). Only the platform host differs. On Android: OpenGL ES 3.0 through EGL, cutscenes decoded by the system MediaPlayer straight into a SurfaceTexture, sound through miniaudio and OpenSL ES, touch controls with a layout editor, and data_vita.win assembled on the phone from your own data.win and the data_vita.patch inside the APK. On the Vita the same job is done by vitaGL, SceAvPlayer, OpenAL and a Windows patcher on the PC.
The runtime, and what differs from the Vita build

The buttons, the D-Pad and the stick are drawn on screen. They can be dragged, resized, made transparent and bound to any gamepad button or key, and the portrait and landscape layouts are stored separately. The pad is a full controller (Xbox or PlayStation scheme, switched on the pause screen) and presents itself to the game as a real pad, so the game shows its own controller prompts. In game, the pause menu opens the same editor.

Butterscotch — the free GameMaker runtime (github.com/ButterscotchRunner/Butterscotch), AGPL-3.0. FreeType (FTL), Box2D, miniaudio, stb and other libraries — see NOTICE.md in the repository. The game and its content belong to their owners: this port does not distribute the game and is not affiliated with its authors.
This Android port exists thanks to the PS Vita port by conop-8888: github.com/conop-8888/avgn-8bit-vita. Without it there would be no Android build.
